newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 11.

text.p: These were the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Police seek army help to conduct March 21 poll in districts bordering northern and eastern provinces. The election will not be held in the two provinces, where separatist Tamil rebels are fighting the military.
Foreign poll monitors will not be invited to the election, despite requests made by some contesting parties, Elections Department sources say.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga, addressing an election rally, promises more than 24,000 private sector jobs for high school qualified youth.
Ceylon Chamber of Commerce and London Chamber of Commerce sign memorandum of understanding to promote trade and business links between Sri Lanka and Britain.

Government doctors plan another nationwide strike next Friday as their demands for salary rivision has not been met by health authorities, the powerful Government Medical Officers Association says. Doctors went on strike on March 5 protesting same issue.
Military intelligence uncover plan by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) to assassinate Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte and army commander Rohan Daluwatte in downtown Colombo.
Campaigning for March 21 local government election must end by midnight on March 18, Elections Department says.
Election results to be updated on the Internet too, Elections Commissioner Dayananda Dissanayake says.
